title: Treasure in Clay Jars
subtitle: 1 & 2 Corinthians in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
Paul's letters to Corinth were written to a young, quarreling church in a busy port city of workshops, markets, and temples. They hold a cross that looks like foolishness, a field where one plants and another waters, a foundation laid once, a table where no one should eat first, one body with many parts, a love that is patient, a seed that dies and rises, a lamp of glory carried in a clay jar, a tent waiting for a house, a poor church giving gladly, and a thorn that did not go away.

This book walks through them in forty short poems, in five parts: three for First Corinthians and two for Second Corinthians. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture. The pictures stay with the things of a working city—a potter's wheel, a bronze mirror, a loaf, a tentmaker's needle, a harbor at dawn—and leave the faces to your imagination.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open Paul's letters to the Corinthians alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

paintings.title: the word of the cross
paintings.epigraph: “For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are dying, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.”
paintings.poem:
a city of speakers.
philosophers on the steps,
everyone with an argument.

and Paul arrives
with a story
about a man
nailed to wood.

it sounded like losing.

but some who heard it
went home
and could not stop
thinking about it.

foolishness,
to the ones walking away.

power,
to the ones being carried home.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the word of the cross” (1 Corinthians 1:18)—where the poem notes, “power, to the ones being carried home”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the weak things
paintings.epigraph: “God chose the weak things of the world that he might put to shame the things that are strong.”
paintings.poem:
look around the room,
Paul says.

not many scholars.
not many rulers.
not many names
anyone would carve in stone.

a dockhand.
a servant girl.
a man who mends sandals.

this is who God picked.

not because
the strong were too good
to be chosen,

but so no one
would ever mistake
who did the saving.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the weak things” (1 Corinthians 1:26–28)—where the poem notes, “would ever mistake who did the saving”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: in fear and much trembling
paintings.epigraph: “I was with you in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling.”
paintings.poem:
he didn't walk in
like a conqueror.

he walked in
with shaking hands.

no polished speech.
no clever proof.

just one thing
he had decided
to know:

Jesus,
and him crucified.

if you are afraid
of the thing
God is asking you to say,

you are in
good company.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What anxious weight can you place into the hands of the One who says, “Be still” and walks beside you in 1 Corinthians 2:1–3?

paintings.title: no eye has seen
paintings.epigraph: “Things which an eye didn’t see, and an ear didn’t hear, which didn’t enter into the heart of man, these God has prepared for those who love him.”
paintings.poem:
you have seen the sea
at sunrise.
you have heard a child laugh
in the next room.

and still,

no eye has seen it.
no ear has heard it.
no heart has pictured it:

what he has made ready
for those who love him.

hold the best morning
you remember.

it is only
the doorway.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “no eye has seen” (1 Corinthians 2:9–10)—where the poem notes, “it is only the doorway”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the increase
paintings.epigraph: “I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase.”
paintings.poem:
they were picking sides.
Paul's people.
Apollos's people.

Paul points at a garden.

I put the seed in.
he brought the water.

neither of us
made anything grow.

some of us plant.
some of us water.
most of us never see
the harvest.

that's all right.

the green
was never
ours to make.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the increase” (1 Corinthians 3:5–7)—where the poem notes, “was never ours to make”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the foundation
paintings.epigraph: “For no one can lay any other foundation than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.”
paintings.poem:
the foundation
is already down.
cut true.
it isn't going anywhere.

what you build on it
is up to you:
gold, or straw.

one day the fire
will walk through
every house.

so build slowly,
with what lasts,

and remember
the ground you stand on
was never
yours to lay.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the foundation” (1 Corinthians 3:10–13)—where the poem notes, “was never yours to lay”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: with our own hands
paintings.epigraph: “W e toil, working with our own hands. When people curse us, we bless.”
paintings.poem:
by day
he stitched tent cloth.

by night
he wrote letters
with the same
tired hands.

hungry sometimes.
no house of his own.

and when they cursed him,
he blessed them.

no one was watching.

just a needle,
a lamp,
and a curse
answered with a blessing,
one stitch at a time.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “with our own hands” (1 Corinthians 4:11–13)—where the poem notes, “answered with a blessing, one stitch at a time”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the new loaf
paintings.epigraph: “Purge out the old yeast, that you may be a new lump”
paintings.poem:
a little yeast
works through
the whole lump.

you can't keep
just a pinch
of the old ways.

so sweep the house.
start a new batch.

Christ, our Passover,
has already been given.
the feast is set.

come with plain bread:
nothing hidden in it,
nothing puffed up,
just true.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: How has God quietly provided enough for today’s road, and who might you welcome to your table in kindness (1 Corinthians 5:6–8)?

paintings.title: but you were washed
paintings.epigraph: “Some of you were such, but you were washed.”
paintings.poem:
some of you
were such.

Paul doesn't pretend
the past
didn't happen.

but he doesn't
leave you there.

but you were washed.
but you were set apart.
but you were made right.

three buts.

every one
a door
out of the old room.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “but you were washed” (1 Corinthians 6:11)—where the poem notes, “a door out of the old room”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: a temple
paintings.epigraph: “don’t you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you”
paintings.poem:
Corinth was full of temples.
marble.
incense.
priests at the door.

and Paul says:
you.

these hands.
these tired feet.
this ordinary body.

the Holy Spirit
lives here.

you are not
a rented room.

you are
a holy place.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “a temple” (1 Corinthians 6:19)—where the poem notes, “you are a holy place”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: bought
paintings.epigraph: “Y ou are not your own, for you were bought with a price.”
paintings.poem:
in the market square
people were sold.
everyone knew
what a price meant.

you are not your own,
Paul says,

and for once
that isn't bad news.

someone paid everything.

you belong now,
not to the market,

but to the one
who walked in
and bought you
out of it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “bought” (1 Corinthians 6:19–20)—where the poem notes, “and bought you out of it”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: love builds up
paintings.epigraph: “Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.”
paintings.poem:
you might be right.

you might know
the idol is nothing,
the meat is only meat.

but knowing
can swell a heart
like dough left too long.

love asks
a different question:

not, am I right?
but, will my brother
still be standing
when I'm done?

knowledge fills a room.

love builds one.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If you were to set down one stone of remembrance today for how God has helped you thus far (1 Corinthians 8:1–3), what would you name it?

paintings.title: the race
paintings.epigraph: “Run like that, that you may win.”
paintings.poem:
they trained for months
for a crown of leaves
that browned in a week.

Paul watched them.

the early mornings.
the plain food.
the aching legs.

run like that,
he says.

not for the leaves.

for a crown
that never
dries up.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the race” (1 Corinthians 9:24–25)—where the poem notes, “that never dries up”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the way out
paintings.epigraph: “God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape”
paintings.poem:
you are not
the first.

what pulls at you
has pulled at others.
it is common.
it is human.

and God is faithful.

he won't let it
be more
than you can carry.

look.

there is a gate
at the end of this alley.

it was there
before you arrived.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the way out” (1 Corinthians 10:13)—where the poem notes, “it was there before you arrived”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: wait for one another
paintings.epigraph: “Do this in memory of me.”
paintings.poem:
some came early
and ate their fill.

some came late, from work,
and found the bowls
already empty.

this is the table
of the one who gave
his body, broken.

no one eats first here.

so set the loaf
in the middle.

wait
for the last one
through the door.

remember him
by leaving room.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In the quiet after the noise, what gentle truth from 1 Corinthians 11:21–26 (“remember him by leaving room”) is asking for your unhurried attention today?

paintings.title: many members
paintings.epigraph: “The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,””
paintings.poem:
the foot says,
I'm not a hand,
so I don't belong.

the eye looks down
at the hand and says,
we don't need you.

both are wrong.

a body
is not one thing
said loudly.

it's many things
held together.

the part of you
you think doesn't matter

is the part
someone else
is leaning on.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “many members” (1 Corinthians 12:14–21)—where the poem notes, “someone else is leaning on”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: love is patient
paintings.epigraph: “Love is patient and is kind.”
paintings.poem:
Corinth worked in bronze.
you could hear it
from the street.

all noise,
Paul says,
if there's no love in it.

love is patient.
it waits for the slow one.

love is kind.
it saves you the last piece.

it keeps no ledger.
it doesn't need to win.
it bears, believes,
hopes, holds on.

quiet work, mostly.

more like bread
than bells.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In the quiet after the noise, what gentle truth from 1 Corinthians 13:1–7 (“more like bread than bells”) is asking for your unhurried attention today?

paintings.title: dimly
paintings.epigraph: “For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face.”
paintings.poem:
the mirrors of that day
were polished bronze.

even the best of them
gave back
only a blur.

that's how we see now.

a shape.
a warmth.
enough to know
someone is there.

but a day is coming
with no bronze
between us.

and I will know him
the way
he has always
known me.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “dimly” (1 Corinthians 13:12)—where the poem notes, “he has always known me”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: what I am
paintings.epigraph: “But by the grace of God I am what I am.”
paintings.poem:
last of all,
he says,
he appeared to me too.

the late one.
the one who
fought against him.

not worthy
of the name.

and still:

by the grace of God
I am what I am.

no better story
to tell about yourself.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “what I am” (1 Corinthians 15:8–10)—where the poem notes, “no better story to tell about yourself”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the seed
paintings.epigraph: “that which you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.”
paintings.poem:
how are the dead raised?
someone asks.
what kind of body?

Paul holds up
a grain of wheat.

bare.
dry.
small.

you bury it.

you don't expect
a grain to come back.

you expect
a field.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the seed” (1 Corinthians 15:36–38)—where the poem notes, “you expect a field”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: where is your sting
paintings.epigraph: ““Death, where is your sting? Hades, where is your victory?””
paintings.poem:
death,
where is your sting?

Paul taunts it
like a bee
that has already
spent itself.

it can still buzz.
it can still frighten.

but the sting
went into Christ,
and stayed there.

swallowed up,
he says.

like a spark
in the sea.

thanks be to God.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “where is your sting” (1 Corinthians 15:54–57)—where the poem notes, “thanks be to God”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: not in vain
paintings.epigraph: “your labor is not in vain in the Lord.”
paintings.poem:
the bowls you shaped
that no one thanked you for.

the prayers
that seemed to go nowhere.

the long
unnoticed Tuesday.

stand firm,
Paul says.
keep at it.

because the one
who raised Christ
from the dead

wastes
nothing.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “not in vain” (1 Corinthians 15:58)—where the poem notes, “wastes nothing”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the God of all comfort
paintings.epigraph: “the Father of mercies and God of all comfort”
paintings.poem:
he doesn't say
the God of some comfort.

or the God of comfort
for small troubles.

all comfort.

and it doesn't stop
with you.

the comfort
he poured into your worst week

is the comfort
you'll carry
to someone else's.

nothing
you've been held through

is wasted.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the God of all comfort” (2 Corinthians 1:3–4)—where the poem notes, “is wasted”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: yes
paintings.epigraph: “For however many are the promises of God, in him is the “Yes.””
paintings.poem:
they said Paul
couldn't make up his mind.
yes, then no.

fine, he says.
look at Jesus.

every promise God ever made:

yes.

in him.

not maybe.
not later.
not yes-and-no.

and all we add
is the amen.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “yes” (2 Corinthians 1:19–20)—where the poem notes, “and all we add is the amen”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the aroma
paintings.epigraph: “For we are a sweet aroma of Christ to God”
paintings.poem:
you can't see it.
you can't hold it.

but walk into a room
where bread is baking

and you know.

that's what he says
we are:

a scent of Christ,
carried from street to street.

not a lecture.

more like
someone opened
a door
somewhere warm.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the aroma” (2 Corinthians 2:14–15)—where the poem notes, “a door somewhere warm”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: a letter
paintings.epigraph: “You are our letter, written in our hearts, known and read by all men”
paintings.poem:
do we need
letters of reference?
Paul asks.

no.
you are the letter.

not ink on papyrus.
not chisel on stone.

the Spirit
writing on hearts.

people read you
without knowing it:
at the market,
on the dock,
at your table.

let them find
his handwriting.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “a letter” (2 Corinthians 3:2–3)—where the poem notes, “let them find his handwriting”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: unveiled
paintings.epigraph: “But whenever someone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.”
paintings.poem:
Moses came down the mountain
shining,
and covered his face
with a cloth,

so no one would watch
the glory fade.

but turn
toward the Lord,
and the cloth
comes away.

we look at him
with open faces,

and slowly,
from glory to glory,

we start
to shine the same.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “unveiled” (2 Corinthians 3:16–18)—where the poem notes, “we start to shine the same”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: out of darkness
paintings.epigraph: “seeing it is God who said, “Light will shine out of darkness,””
paintings.poem:
the same voice
that said
let there be light

over the dark water
at the beginning

has said it
again

over the dark water
in you.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “out of darkness” (2 Corinthians 4:6)—where the poem notes, “over the dark water in you”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: clay jars
paintings.epigraph: “the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God, and not from ourselves.”
paintings.poem:
the potters' street
was full of them.
cheap jars.
common clay.

that's what we are,
Paul says.

and the treasure
is inside:

the light of God's glory
in something
that could break.

so no one
mistakes the jar
for the light.

and if you're cracked,

that's just
where it gets out.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “clay jars” (2 Corinthians 4:7)—where the poem notes, “that's just where it gets out”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: not crushed
paintings.epigraph: “W e are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair”
paintings.poem:
pressed,
but not crushed.

confused,
but not hopeless.

chased,
but not left alone.

knocked down,
but not finished.

read it
one more time,

slowly,

and lean
on the second half
of every line.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you pause at the threshold of “not crushed” (2 Corinthians 4:8–9), what closed place in your life is waiting for you to open to His presence?

paintings.title: day by day
paintings.epigraph: “though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day.”
paintings.poem:
the knees ache more.
the eyes need more light.
the jar is wearing thin
at the edges.

and still,
every morning,

something inside
is being filled
again.

don't keep your eyes
only on the jar.

what you can see
is for a while.

what you can't
is forever.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “day by day” (2 Corinthians 4:16–18)—where the poem notes, “what you can't is forever”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the tent and the house
paintings.epigraph: “we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal, in the heavens.”
paintings.poem:
a tentmaker
knows tents.

how the cloth thins.
how the pegs pull loose.
how the wind
finds every hole.

this body, he says,
is a tent.

we groan in it.
we're tired in it.

but there's a house
not made with hands,

already built,
waiting,

with a light on.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In the quiet after the noise, what gentle truth from 2 Corinthians 5:1–4 (“with a light on”) is asking for your unhurried attention today?

paintings.title: new
paintings.epigraph: “Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.”
paintings.poem:
not patched.
not repainted.
not improved.

new.

the old things
passed away.

look,

he says,
like a man
showing you a field
after rain.

everything
has become new.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “new” (2 Corinthians 5:17)—where the poem notes, “everything has become new”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: ambassadors
paintings.epigraph: “We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ”
paintings.poem:
an ambassador
doesn't speak
for himself.

he carries
someone else's word
across the water.

and the word is this:

God was in Christ,
making peace with the world,
not counting what we'd done.

so we carry it
to the dock,
the shop,
the kitchen table:

come home.

he is not counting.
he is asking.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “ambassadors” (2 Corinthians 5:18–20)—where the poem notes, “he is not counting. he is asking”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: having nothing
paintings.epigraph: “as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.”
paintings.poem:
unknown,
and well known.

dying,
and look, we live.

sad,
and always rejoicing.

poor,
and making many rich.

empty-handed,

and holding
everything.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “having nothing” (2 Corinthians 6:8–10)—where the poem notes, “and holding everything”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the Macedonians
paintings.epigraph: “the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded to the riches of their generosity.”
paintings.poem:
they had almost nothing.

trouble all around.
poverty deep
as a well.

and they begged Paul
to let them give.

beyond what they could.
more than anyone asked.

first they gave themselves
to the Lord.

the coins
just followed.

joy
is a strange thing.

sometimes it grows best
in the poorest soil.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the Macedonians” (2 Corinthians 8:1–5)—where the poem notes, “sometimes it grows best in the poorest soil”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: a cheerful giver
paintings.epigraph: “God loves a cheerful giver.”
paintings.poem:
a farmer
who holds back seed
for fear of losing it
stands in a thin field.

the one who throws it wide
walks home through gold.

so give
the way you'd scatter seed:

not pinched.
not pushed.
open-handed.

maybe even smiling,

knowing
who fills the sack.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What anxious weight can you place into the hands of the One who says, “Be still” and walks beside you in 2 Corinthians 9:6–7?

paintings.title: the basket
paintings.epigraph: “I was let down in a basket through a window by the wall, and escaped his hands.”
paintings.poem:
others were boasting
of their pedigree,
their visions,
their credentials.

and Paul tells them
about the basket.

the night he was lowered
over the Damascus wall
like laundry,

folded up,
hiding,
getting away.

if I have to boast,
he says,

I'll boast
about that.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the basket” (2 Corinthians 11:30–33)—where the poem notes, “I'll boast about that”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the thorn
paintings.epigraph: “Concerning this thing, I begged the Lord three times that it might depart from me.”
paintings.poem:
he asked
three times.

take it away.
take it away.
take it away.

and heaven
did not say no
like a closed door.

heaven said:

my grace is enough
for you.

he never tells us
what the thorn was.

maybe
so each of us
could lay our own
beside it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the thorn” (2 Corinthians 12:7–9)—where the poem notes, “could lay our own beside it”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: when I am weak
paintings.epigraph: “For when I am weak, then am I strong.”
paintings.poem:
we pray to be strong
so we won't need him.

he lets us be weak
so we'll find out
he's there.

the power
rests
on the empty places.

the open jar
fills.

so let the weakness stay
if it must.

it is
where his strength
